messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: HIGH - model-inference-canary errors increased above threshold for model/redwood-v2-quantized at 03:24 UTC. Calling oncall group.

sre-bot: Alerts: 500x spike in model error rate on canary pool; latency up ~2x; tokens-per-request unchanged. Sampling shows incorrect token boundaries in outputs.

alex: I'm on it — grabbing logs from the canary cluster. Which weightset did we push last night?

maria: rollout id r-2026-04-15-qconv, weightset wset-20260415-q4. Jenkins shows conversion job finished OK but there were a couple warnings: "quantize: outlier scale clipped".

jin: fyi I saw small diffs in tokenized lengths for some prompts in QA after deploy. Might be tokenizer config drift or quantization introducing numerical differences that change BPE boundaries.

emily: attaching quick sample: 
```
input: "Can you summarize the PR?"
old tokenization: [Can, you, summarize, the, PR, ?]
new tokenization: [Can, you, summar, ize, the, PR, ?]
model output: broken mid-word tokens and occasional garbled tokens.
```

rahul: Repro on canary VM: when we force fp16 decode it looks OK. With q4 decode it breaks. Suspect misquantized weightset.

alex: Can we flip the quantization feature flag to force fallback to fp16 for canary? That should mitigate customer impact while we investigate.

maria: Flipping flag now: /dd feature-flag set inference.quantize_enabled=false --env canary

deploy-bot: Executing feature-flag change. Rolling to 12 canary nodes.

deploy-bot: Completed: inference.quantize_enabled=false on canary (12 nodes).

alex: Observability - latency climbed briefly during the rollout but errors dropped to baseline within 30s. Good call.

jin: Starting deeper inspection: comparing wset-20260415-q4 to last known-good wset-20260414-q4. Hash mismatch in several shards. Looks like conversion script changed rounding rules.

emily: Confirmed: per-layer scale tensors differ. Some scales are zero-clipped in the new bundle which causes token misalignment during softmax -> decoding.

sre-bot: Customer impact: a small set (~0.8% of requests) on canary were returning malformed tokens, causing degraded responses. No data exfil.

liz: Product - are there paying customers on canary? We need a customer impact statement.

alex: A/B canary group includes a staging account and a small set of enterprise trials. We flagged 3 accounts for potential noisy outputs. Notifying CSMs now.

rahul: Ops suggestion: rollback weightset to wset-20260414-stable on canary then re-run conversion with stricter clipping tests.

maria: Initiating rollback: /deploy rollback model redwood-v2-quantized --target wset-20260414-stable --scope canary

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued. Running preflight checks...

deploy-bot: Rollback in progress: replacing 12 canary nodes weights -> approx 3m ETA

sre-bot: Monitoring: errors trending down as nodes finish replacement. Latency normalizing.

jin: Will fork the quantization pipeline, add numeric diff test comparing tokenization boundaries across quant levels and fail conversion when BPE boundaries shift.

emily: I'll open a patch to the conversion script to preserve scale precision and add unit tests for the specific layers that clipped.

liz: CSMs notified. Messaging template: "We observed an issue with a canary weight conversion that caused incorrect token outputs for a small set of requests. We've rolled the canary back and disabled quantization on canary nodes while we root cause. No customer data was exposed; impact limited. We'll follow up with a timeline."

alex: Oncall notes: keep flag disabled for canary until new conversion passes the diff tests. Plan to re-run conversion in a staging environment with canary-like inputs.

maria: Postmortem assignee: jin + emily. Timeline: quick fix + tests by EOD; full postmortem and deploy-safe checklist by EOD+2.

rahul: Any need to do Dedicated or Hosted rollout holds? Recommend hold on global qconv until patch verified.

alex: Putting global rollout on hold via release manager. /dd release hold qconv-global-2026-04-15

deploy-bot: Release held: qconv-global-2026-04-15.

sre-bot: Closing pager: error rate returned to baseline, mitigation in place (rollback + feature flag). Please follow up with postmortem and test coverage.

oncall-bot: Pager resolved by oncall (alex). If further anomalies occur reopen with thread ts 2003456789. :white_check_mark:
